The RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation is a professional graphics card by NVIDIA, launched on March 18th, 2025. Built on the 5 nm process, and based on the GB202GL graphics processor, in its GB202-870-A1 variant, the card supports DirectX 12 Ultimate. The GB202GL graphics processor is a very large chip with a die area of 750 mm² and 92.2 billion transistors. It features 24064 shading units, 752 texture mapping units, and 192 ROPs. Also included are 752 Tensor Cores which help improve the speed of machine learning applications with support for the FP4, FP6, INT8 and FP8 data formats. The GPU also has 188 raytracing acceleration cores. NVIDIA has paired 96 GB GDDR7 memory with the RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation, which is connected using a 512-bit memory interface. The GPU is operating at a frequency of 1590 MHz, which can be boosted up to 2617 MHz, memory is running at 1750 MHz (28 Gbps effective).
Being a dual-slot card, the NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation draws power from 1x 16-pin power connector, with power draw rated at 600 W maximum. Display outputs include: 4x DisplayPort 2.1b. RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation is connected to the rest of the system using a PCI-Express 5.0 x16 interface. The card's dimensions are 304 mm x 137 mm x 40 mm, and it features a dual-slot cooling solution. Its price at launch was 8,565 US Dollars.
